featured_techniques.technique: Hire memory makers and assess memory-creating ability via storytelling
Cruise director / navigator guiding through complexity to create memory and peace of mind

sections.description: Define the start and end moments of customer interactions (hellos and goodbyes) as bookends. Engage mid-level staff to brainstorm these moments, determine which rituals belong to the experience, consider whether some elements should be delegated to a rhythmic service, and push to shed legacy industry practices in favor of a more personal connection.
sections.title: Action 1 — Establish bookend customer experiences

concepts: business growth linked to peace of mind
sections.description: During hires, seek candidates who can create memory and reveal it through stories or demonstrations. Look for the 'light behind the eye' as an indicator. Position the organization with a 'cruise director' or navigator who guides customers through complexity, with the resulting memories delivering peace of mind that fuels business growth.
sections.title: Action 2–3 — Hire memory makers and appoint a cruise director

summary: In a concise 98-second talk, Jeanne Bliss outlines three actions to embed clarity of purpose into a business. She advocates starting with bookend customer experiences to engage mid-level staff in shaping the most meaningful entry and exit moments, challenging legacy practices, and pushing for a more personal connection with customers. She then emphasizes hiring for memory-making ability—looking for candidates who can create memorable moments and demonstrate it in storytelling or a concrete example. Finally, she pitches the role of a cruise director or navigator who guides customers through organizational complexity, with the guidance turning into memory that delivers peace of mind and, in turn, drives business growth.
title: Three Actions to Build Clarity of Purpose in Your Organization (Jeanne Bliss)
topics: Light behind the eye (memory-building interview cue)
